{"id": "aa5ac827-03fc-41be-84d3-aea7924d1936", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I can share a straightforward CloudFormation template for an S3 bucket, but a couple of things worth flagging first:

- I can give you the template text here in chat.
- If you'd like it saved as a persistent artifact (so you can view/update it later), I can create one — just let me know.
- I don't have the ability to actually deploy/apply CloudFormation stacks to your account from here — I can give you the YAML/JSON, but deploying it would need to happen through your own CI/CD or the console/CLI.

Here's a solid baseline template with sensible defaults (encryption, versioning, public access block):

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: S3 bucket with encryption, versioning, and public access blocked

Parameters:
  BucketName:
    Type: String
    Description: Name for the S3 bucket (must be globally unique). Leave blank to let CloudFormation generate one.
    Default: ""

Conditions:
  HasBucketName: !Not [!Equals [!Ref BucketName, ""]]

Resources:
  S3Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !If [HasBucketName, !Ref BucketName, !Ref "AWS::NoValue"]
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

Outputs:
  BucketName:
    Description: Name of the created S3 bucket
    Value: !Ref S3Bucket
  BucketArn:
    Description: ARN of the created S3 bucket
    Value: !GetAtt S3Bucket.Arn
```

Notes:
- `DeletionPolicy: Retain` prevents accidental data loss if the stack is deleted — remove it if you want the bucket deleted along with the stack.
- Add a `LifecycleConfiguration` if you need expiration/transition rules, or `LoggingConfiguration` for access logs — happy to extend this if you need those.
